annotations.annotation_text: ALP invocation "Liffey" on page 576 ("The Bedroom Scene"): Anna Livia Plurabelle, the mother-river personifying the Liffey, surfaces here amid HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream. In this Age of Men (closing) passage, her feminine current of forgiveness and renewal flows through the dream landscape, carrying Dublin's history from source to sea.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Hart, Clive. Structure and Motif in Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/structuremotifin0000hart

annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "sleep" on page 576 ("The Bedroom Scene"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream. During this Age of Men (closing) phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish

annotations.annotation_text: HCE manifestation "builder" on page 576 within "The Bedroom Scene": here the universal father-figure Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker appears in the context of HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream. During this Age of Men (closing) phase, HCE embodies the patriarch whose guilt, grandeur, and fall drive the cyclical dream forward.
